title: Cheat curls: EZ bar vs Dumbbells
summary: NH, who credits seven years of cheat curls for his biceps, compares cheat curls with an EZ bar and with dumbbells. EZ bar cheat curls turn into supinated cleans driven by technique and hips and stress the shoulder, so negatives are better done on a preacher bench. Dumbbell cheat curls, done alternating with weight in both hands and starting from a neutral grip, force a real curl finish and are his preferred method.
claims: Do both EZ bar and dumbbell curls in general; this comparison concerns only cheat curls
He has done cheat curls for seven years, never missing a session, and they are what grew his biceps
He only shares methods he has personally used and seen work
With EZ bar cheat curls the weight climbs through neural and technical adaptation rather than biceps growth, turning them into supinated cleans
A curl is an isolation movement, not a compound; if you feel other muscles as much as the biceps you are doing it wrong
Olympic lifts build less muscle than typical compounds because they lack a controlled eccentric and are highly technical
People who cheat curl three plates with a supinated grip don't have biceps strong enough to curl that weight; it is whole-body explosiveness
The only redeeming part of an EZ bar cheat curl is a controlled negative, but you can get that more easily on a preacher bench or with heavy single-arm negatives assisted on the way up
EZ bar cheat curls often become a shoulder shrug and swing that can overextend and injure the shoulder
On EZ bar curls keep the elbows by your sides; the bar should come nowhere near your forehead
Dumbbell cheat curls cap the usable load, keep the weight close to the body and physically force a proper curl finish because you can't swing it to your face
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and alternate; the other dumbbell stabilizes you, while an empty free hand lets you contort like an Olympic lift
Dumbbell cheat technique: use a leg drive to throw the dumbbell through the range you couldn't curl, then catch it and finish the top partial with the biceps
Start curls from a neutral grip and supinate on the way up; it reduces front delt involvement, adds forearm work and lowers rotator cuff and biceps tear risk
Cheat curls should be at least 3 reps with 1 rep in reserve; one-rep maxes are useless
He doesn't deliberately slow the negative on cheat curls; a fast but controlled lowering still keeps tension and stretch and is safe
Start cheat curls very light; anyone without much biceps training experience should stick to normal curls
exercises: weight in both hands, alternate; start neutral then supinate; leg drive then finish top with biceps; fast controlled negative; 3+ reps, 1 RIR
forces proper curl, safer, his main biceps builder
elbows by sides, bar away from forehead
becomes a supinated clean; shoulder risk; only negative is valuable
heavy single-arm negative, assist the positive
